step1_analysis.description: A single-to-differential converter based on peak locking, designed to restore the small signal output of an envelope detector while maintaining pulse width integrity for a biomedical retinal prosthesis.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the circuit from the supply.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_VDD. With VDD=1.8V and scaled down transistor lengths (0.5um in sky130 vs 0.5um original), the current should be similar or slightly lower.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Scaled for 1.8V supply in SKY130 compared to the original 2.5V/3V supply.

conversion_gain.description: AC voltage gain from the single-ended input to the output nodes.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = gm * Rout. Depending on the bias current and load, typical single-stage conversion gain is around 10-20 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard expectation for a single-to-differential converter stage.
The circuit must process the 13.56MHz carrier or envelope signals, so bandwidth should exceed this.

transient_swing.description: Peak-to-peak voltage swing at the output nodes.

sky130_expected.calculation: Limited by VDD (1.8V) and VDSAT of the output transistors.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sufficient swing is needed to drive subsequent digital or comparator stages.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC conversion gain, bandwidth, and transient output swing of the single-to-differential converter.
